Note that the following PRs could negatively impact this feature, given they enable compression on resources that are formerly not compressed:

- https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/103284
- https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/103287
- https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/104571
  - This one is on textures which are already compressed, so it's probably not too bad as you're meant to exclude those from delta patching in most cases.

We should consider if we can rely on whole-file PCK compression instead, even when delta patching is not used. (In other words, the base PCK could also use Zstandard compression to make it much smaller than it is right now - similar to what happens when you export with a ZIP data pack instead of PCK).

> - Experiment with the other compression algorithms we have available, maybe even picking the more effective one dynamically, like Android does.

We currently have FastLZ which can be faster than Zstandard, but we don't have [LZ4](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/100866) which is the gold standard when it comes to fast (de)compression, at the cost of worse compression ratio.

That said, Zstandard seems performant enough to me already, given the benchmarks in OP.

> Note that the following PRs could negatively impact this feature, given they enable compression on resources that are formerly not compressed: [...]

So long as the compression is toggleable, like it is with GDScript and `*.translation` files, I think it's mostly fine. There's obviously some amount of balancing between load times, main PCK size and the size of any patch PCK that needs to be considered on a per-project basis.

If possible, we might want to emit some kind of warning when exporting a delta patch and any of these forms of compression is enabled.

> We should consider if we can rely on whole-file PCK compression instead, even when delta patching is not used.

I haven't confirmed this, but I think we'd still want to compress on a per-file basis with delta patches though, even if the PCK as whole was compressed, as both the original bsdiff and Android's fork of it compress the three separate parts (control data, diff data, new data) separately, which I believe is meant to result in a better a compression ratio, as opposed to compressing it all in one go.
I added some of my previous notes on binary diff here https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/13404#issuecomment-3412615809

Thanks to the notes linked above I'll be removing bsdiff in favor of just using zstd's own patching feature instead, where you feed in the old file as the dictionary, which seems to yield very similar size savings compared to bsdiff+zstd, at a fraction of the memory used to create them and (at least at first glance) the time taken applying them as well.

I'm setting this to draft until then.

I've been exploring the zstd-only approach for a bit now, and the wins weren't quite as "across the board" as I originally thought. You can read more about it (and chime in if you want) here: [godotengine/godot-proposals#13404](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/13404#issuecomment-3428936720)

**tl;dr:** bsdiff+zstd seems to apply patches quicker on average, and offers more flexibility to further decrease this cost, so I'm leaning towards going with the bsdiff implementation in this PR (as-is) after all, unless somebody feels strongly that we shouldn't.

> I've been exploring the zstd-only approach for a bit now, and the wins weren't quite as "across the board" as I originally thought. You can read more about it (and chime in if you want) here: [godotengine/godot-proposals#13404](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/13404#issuecomment-3428936720)
> 
> **tl;dr:** bsdiff+zstd seems to apply patches quicker on average, and offers more flexibility to further decrease this cost, so I'm leaning towards going with the bsdiff implementation in this PR (as-is) after all, unless somebody feels strongly that we shouldn't.

@mihe Your comments about memory + maintenance are pulling me toward the zstd-only approach:
- zstd-only having a fixed (?) export memory cost and lower decompression / runtime memory cost makes it an ideal candidate on mobile devices, whether we're talking about compressing using the Android editor, or decompression by an Android game.
- any solution that lowers the maintenance burden is a win in my book

Well, I ended up going with the zstd-only approach after all: #112011

You can read more about why here: [godotengine/godot-proposals#13404](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/13404#issuecomment-3444638520)
